officialSourceAssessment.nationalCustodian: Egyptian Survey Authority (ESA) states that it produces topographic, digital and property-related maps and offers digital map products; its public pages describe ordering maps by location, scale, layers, format and projection.
officialSourceAssessment.localCustodian: Official planning material identifies Abu Qurqas in Minya Governorate and an official public-service entry identifies a survey statement service requiring a governorate/area selection, but no Abu Qurqas-local public cadastral map/API was evidenced.

attemptsRecorded.outcome: ESA history and service overview were reachable; the page describes cadastral/property record and map responsibilities but exposes no anonymous parcel-vector endpoint.
ESA services listed digital maps, coordinate certificates and land-boundary-related services; no public parcel layer URL or schema was exposed.

ESA digital-map page was fetched and inspected. It describes a paid/request workflow for digital maps with selected layers and projection. Linked map pages were static national/administrative maps; no current JavaScript/configuration for parcel querying, WMS/WFS, ArcGIS FeatureServer, or ID-plus-geometry response was found.
ESA map index exposed static PDF maps and an Egypt map page, not cadastral parcel vector data.
ESA directorate page used a static image map; it did not expose parcel geometry or a query API.
Official Gazette material evidenced approval/modification of Abu Qurqas strategic urban planning, not cadastral parcel-vector access.

Search result described an official survey-statement service, but direct TLS request failed certificate validation because the certificate was expired. No TLS exception was attempted. The result did not expose parcel geometry.
GOPP material evidenced Abu Qurqas strategic planning and local planning participation, not a parcel registry viewer or anonymous geometry service.
